guards: Limit lexical readings to the explicitly approved DAR give and DECIR say/tell senses, not hit, occur, passive, idiomatic or unrelated homograph senses.
Exact retained combined-with descriptions and source pronoun/person/number/mood metadata must establish the composition. Never split suffixes or infer an unattested accented spelling.
lo/la -> it and los/las -> them require an explicit selected inanimate/abstract-content reading label. Do not claim that human-object interpretations are covered.
le/les -> him/her/them require selected third-person recipient labels and exact singular/plural constraints; do not silently include formal you or leismo interpretations.

For first/second-person single clitics, source object-person tags alone do not prove dative. Label the bounded give/tell recipient interpretation as a selected model reading rather than source-explicit dative fact; withhold source contexts inconsistent with it.
Double-clitic se may stand for indirect le/les only when that role is explicitly given by the source; preserve separate direct-object number. Never treat single reflexive se as le/les.
Convert first/second-person recipients to reflexive English only after matching actual finite subject person AND number. Formal imperative third-person morphology addresses you, not he/she/they.
For matching plural nos/os, mark the output selected reflexive reading; reciprocal one-another interpretations also exist and are not covered.
Infinitives and gerunds without an explicit subject/controller retain me/you/us rather than invent myself/yourself/ourselves.

DAR recipient-only give him/give me must remain visibly labelled elliptical recipient fragments with unexpressed direct object; give to him is an alternative that preserves the recipient role. Do not assert a complete clause or invent a gift/destination.
DECIR direct-only uses say it/them; recipient-only uses tell me/him/etc.; combined roles use say it/them to recipient. No direct me/te/nos/os templates under these reviewed say/tell senses.
Use the existing exact mood/person/number/tense, positive predicate, AGID sense/unknown-form, aspect and it-only restrictions. No invented object, example sentence or universal-translation claim.

A malformed form_of target may be normalized only for dar/decir combined with an identical explicit clitic description in the same source gloss, with an agreeing explicit of dar/of decir root; no spelling normalization or suffix split is authorized.

Dedicated clitic policy review approves DECIR recipient tell narrowly under the exact retained to say, to tell, to name, to mention source gloss. This does not assert prior general tell-head approval or authorize other lexical tell senses.

rejectedCases.case: DARSE, DESE, DENSE, DÁNDOSE, DECIRSE, DÍGASE, DÍGANSE single-se readings
rejectedCases.reason: Reflexive/passive/idiomatic possibilities are not equivalent to a selected le/les recipient.

rejectedCases.case: NOS DECIMOS interpreted exclusively as we tell ourselves
rejectedCases.reason: Plural nos can be reciprocal; approve only a visibly selected reflexive reading, never a universal interpretation.

rejectedCases.case: DARME or DÁNDOME -> give/giving myself without a controller
rejectedCases.reason: Nonfinite source forms do not identify the giver; me is retained under the selected recipient reading.
This fails the English say/tell argument mapping; direct-person calling/naming senses require separate review.

rejectedCases.case: Unknown/contradictory source roles, unsupported compounds, arbitrary single se, or ambiguous controlled subject
rejectedCases.reason: Withhold rather than repair grammar or infer roles from spelling.

notes: Read all 96 retained senses/80 words and both lemma sense inventories. This is a bounded policy approval with the listed guards, not approval of every source analysis or generated output. Independent model linguistic review, not source quotation or native-Mexican certification. RAE confirms se as le(s) before lo/la/los/las and the reflexive/reciprocal ambiguity of nos/os/se: https://www.rae.es/dpd/se ; https://www.rae.es/gtg/pronombre-rec%C3%ADproco Reviewed all 11 added source analyses individually, for DÍGAME, DÍMELO, DÍSELO, DÁRSELO, DÉMELO, DÁRTELO, DÁRMELO, DÉMELA, DÁRMELA, DÁRTELA and DÍMELA: total 107 senses/91 words. Their malformed targets agree exactly with explicit same-sense lemma/clitic descriptions. Reviewed the current helper policy-hash, source-record binding, narrow tell fallback and nonfinite/reflexive paths; policy approval retains every existing guard.
